prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the top-down egocentric layout where the camera wearer's chin and upper torso at the bottom center are nearest (bright white, ~0.1–0.4 m), their extended arms holding a pink foam board in front-left and a drill in front-right are within arm's reach (~0.4–0.7 m), and the corner walls and floor with a storage bin and shelving on the right are farther below and ahead (~0.8–1.8 m, darker grey to black). No other people are present; the camera wearer faces downward toward the wall corner and floor, with their lower body occluded by their protruding torso and the storage shelving partly out of view on the right edge. Across the five frames, the wearer turns clockwise toward the right while lowering the foam board closer to the left floor/wall (~0.6–0.9 m) and extending the right arm and drill forward into the corner (~0.5 m). The depth map reveals the continuous vertical distance gradient along the wearer's chest, arms, and recessed right-side floor space more clearly than RGB alone, where flat lighting makes the wall and floor planes blend together. However, it is unreliable in frames 3–5 where the flat wall surface above the board turns overly bright (~0.3 m appearance) and the dark right-hand background collapses into uniform black with lost object boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates two primary foreground regions within arm's reach (~0.1–0.8 m): the camera wearer's own torso and arms at the bottom center (labeled 'person') and the rectangular pink foam board held directly in front and to the left of the torso (~0.3–0.6 m away from the chest). No other people are in the scene, and the camera wearer faces downward away from the camera lens while their legs and feet remain occluded beneath their torso and outside the frame. From frame 1 to frame 4, the masks track the foam board rotating counter-clockwise and shifting down and to the left relative to the wearer's torso as the wearer turns clockwise and reaches forward with the right arm. Compared to RGB, the segmentation map sharply delineates the boundary where the wearer's gloved left hand overlaps the bottom edge of the board in frames 1–3, separating foreground silhouette from background clutter. However, the map is highly unreliable in semantics and completeness: it mislabels the foam board as 'umbrella' (frames 1–4) or 'person' (frame 4), completely misses the walls, shelving, floor items, and drill, and drops the main foam board mask entirely in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1 and 2 and provides only sparse keypoints in frames 3–5 for the camera wearer (0.1–0.6 m from the camera), with no other people present in the workspace. In frame 4, a cluster of magenta hand keypoints localizes the wearer's right gloved hand holding the drill in front-center within arm's reach (~0.5 m away, ~0.3 m to the right of the foam board), while yellow torso keypoints in frame 4 outline the wearer's shoulders and hips below the camera as the wearer faces downward toward the corner. Across frames 3 to 5, the appearance and shift of these keypoints reflect the wearer turning clockwise and raising the right hand forward into view before the hand skeleton disappears again in frame 5. When active in frame 4, the pose map explicitly localizes the articulated finger cluster of the black glove against the dark background and drill, which is hard to distinguish in the dark RGB region, and approximates hidden hip positions beneath the bulky sweatshirt. Overall, however, the pose map is severely unreliable for this steep top-down egocentric viewpoint, failing to detect the wearer's body or left hand across most frames and producing a distorted, collapsed torso polygon in frame 4.
